booking.note: Verbatim: 'campsites can, and should be, reserved until 11pm ET on the date of arrival' and 'Indiana is 100% reservable until 11pm ET on the day of arrival' - no sites are held back for walk-ins. Walk-in registration is still accepted on the day of arrival only, with the camper present, but is being phased out and guarantees nothing. Weekend rule: a Friday night must include Thursday or Saturday; a Saturday night must include Friday or Sunday. The One-Night Relaxed Rule waives that for sites still unrented 3 days out, but 'Required holiday minimum stays are excluded from this relaxed rule' - hence two rules, not one.

fees.note: The $15/$7 figure is the park ENTRANCE fee (out-of-state / Indiana plates), not a camping surcharge - Indiana has no non-resident camping rate. For CAMPERS it is effectively once per stay, not daily: 'when staying overnight, you will be required to pay the entrance fee the first time you enter and your receipt or hang tag will serve as your in/out pass the remainder of your stay.' Exceptions: Prophetstown $8/$16, Indiana Dunes $7/$20. A Non-Resident Annual Entrance Pass is $120. FIRSTHAND (AWH, 2026): booking online charges the campsite fee, tax and the $6 reservation fee, and the $15 entrance fee is then collected AT THE GATE on arrival with no mention of it during booking. So the booking total understates a one-night out-of-state stay by 15 dollars - which is why entrance is a separate field and must be added to any quoted cost rather than assumed included. --AWH/--Claude Add-ons (2026-11-07): Tax: rates exclude tax; Indiana state sales tax plus the county innkeeper's tax are added, so the total varies by county. The $6 transaction fee is charged on web and phone reservations, never on walk-in registrations in the field. Six people a site at most. One vehicle a site at most properties (very few allow two); extra vehicles park in overflow lots and each pays its own entrance fee. Weekend rates (Thursday-Saturday) run +$3 non-electric, +$7 electric, +$10 full hookup and +$0 primitive over Sunday-Wednesday, with a higher holiday-weekend column, so no single flat premium fits the row.

booking.note: DELIBERATELY THIN - federal is the one ownership where an agency default helps LEAST, and treating it like a state row would be the most expensive mistake in the registry (3,738 entries). Federal camping policy is set per FACILITY, not per agency: the 6-month rolling window at 10:00 ET is the recreation.gov standard, but group sites often open 12 months out and some BLM/USFS facilities use 14- or 30-day windows, and FCFS varies campground by campground - many USACE and USFS sites are entirely first-come. So fcfs and min_stay are absent here on purpose rather than defaulted. The right instrument for federal entries is the per-facility recreation.gov availability walk (docs/campground-schema.md phase 4), which answers season and FCFS from the calendar itself; this row exists only to supply the handful of facts that really are agency-wide. Note the doc's estimate of '3,738 entries from ~6-10 rows' was optimistic for exactly this reason.

fees.note: No resident/non-resident distinction exists on federal land. Add-ons (2026-11-07): Reservation fee: recreation.gov's site-wide policy says a reservation fee 'may be charged' ($8 online, $9 call centre, $3 in person), and whether it is depends on the agency: the Forest Service, BLM and others pass it on, while the Corps (by policy) and the Park Service (park by park) fold the cost into the nightly fee and charge none. So it is set on the agency rows, not here. Changing an individual-campsite reservation to dates entirely outside the original costs $10; extending or shortening it is free. A cancellation keeps back a $10 service fee. Cancelling the day before or the day of arrival costs $10 plus the first night (all of it for a one-night stay). The reservation fee itself is never refunded. Tax: not settled for federal campgrounds as a whole. Federally run fee campgrounds post untaxed FLREA fees, but concessionaire-run ones add state and local tax: the Forest Service's Pines Campground (Stanislaus) posts '$33.00 per night (+fees and taxes)', and Yellowstone's concession campgrounds post '+ taxes'. Non-resident: since 2026-01-01 eleven national parks charge non-US residents a $100 entrance surcharge. That is an entrance charge, not a camping rate, and it doesn't touch any US state's residents.

discounts.note: America the Beautiful Senior and Access passes, per NPS: 'The Senior Pass may provide a 50 percent discount on some amenity fees charged for facilities and services such as camping, swimming, boat launch, and specialized interpretive services', honored by NPS, USFWS, USFS, BLM, Bureau of Reclamation and USACE. NOTE THE AGENCY'S OWN HEDGE - 'may' and 'some'. The discount is real and worth asking about at any federally operated campground, but it is discretionary per site, so treat this as 'ask', not 'guaranteed'. The standard $80 Annual Pass carries NO camping discount, which is a common and expensive assumption.

booking.note: The strongest walk-up wording found anywhere: 'Campsites that cannot be reserved are offered on a first come, first served basis. In many cases, reservable sites that have not been booked can also be used on a first come, first served basis.' Booking shuts early - 'most reservations can only be made up until 8 pm two days before your arrival date' - but with a caveat no other agency has: 'Parks that have internet connectivity accept reservations right up until your planned arrival date.' So the cutoff is a function of whether the park has a signal, not of policy, and reserve_until holds the conservative two-day figure. THE WINDOW CHANGED FOR 2026: three months, down from four; anything citing four months is stale. Released 7am Pacific daily. Statutory holiday weekends need three nights. MAX STAY IS PER CALENDAR YEAR, not per visit - 'At most parks, you can stay a maximum of 14 nights each calendar year in total (consecutive or non-consecutive)', and seven at sWiWs and Porteau Cove. That is a different kind of limit from everywhere else in this registry and max_stay_nights cannot express it; read the note.

fees.note: Reservation fee '$6 per campsite per night, to a maximum of $18 per site (plus tax)'; phone adds a $5 per-transaction surcharge; first-come sites have none. Since May 15, 2026, people who do not live in B.C. pay a $20 non-resident fee 'per party per campground' - reserved or first come, first served - shown at booking or paid in the park without proof of B.C. residency. Fees vary by park and season: peak (summer) June 15 to Labour Day, higher at 59 high-use parks; shoulder; and a winter rate at some. Each campground's fees are on its entry. Cancelling more than seven days out refunds camping fees but never the transaction fees. NOTE on rating.price_tier for Canadian entries: the imported RV Life tier is computed on nominal dollars with no CAD conversion, so Canadian parks sit roughly one level high - see docs/campground-schema.md 4.3. Add-ons (2026-11-07): No park entry fee: the camping fee covers the site and parking for one vehicle (some busy parks need a free day-use pass for day visitors). Camping fees and the non-resident fee include tax; the transaction fees (reservation, change, cancellation, call-centre surcharge) have tax added. The non-resident fee is $20 per party per campground, reserved or first come, and not charged for children or youth. A second vehicle pays 50% of the base camping fee, up to $12 a night; further vehicles are set by the park operator. A camping party is at least one adult (16+), no more than four adults and no more than eight people in all; the fee is per party, not per person. No weekend or holiday premium is published; fees vary by park and by peak season (June 15 to Labour Day).

fees.note: Each campground's fees are set by market demand and services within the approved range: basic campsites $8-31 a night, plus $8 a night each for water, electric and sewer hook-ups (and for showers where they are not coin-operated); GST included. A non-refundable $12 reservation fee per reservation, online or by phone; first-come sites have none. No day-use fee and no out-of-province rate difference, but vehicles parked in Kananaskis Country and the Bow Valley need a Kananaskis Conservation Pass ($15 a day, $90 a year; on those entries). Each campground's prices are on its entry. See the BC row's note on Canadian rating.price_tier being roughly one level high. Add-ons (2026-11-07): No day-use or entry fee in provincial parks, except that vehicles parked at provincial parks and public land sites in Kananaskis Country and the Bow Valley Corridor need a Kananaskis Conservation Pass ($15 a day for one vehicle, $90 a year; trailers and extra passengers free; McLean Creek and Fisher Creek PRAs exempt); camping fees do not include it, and it is on the entries that need it. Fees include GST (Alberta has no PST) unless a campground says otherwise; some concession-run campgrounds post prices before tax. The $12 reservation fee is the same online and by phone; changes are $10 online, $5 per amendment for phone-in reservations. A campsite may hold at most three camping units, motor vehicles and towed equipment in all, only two of them used for sleeping; a second camping fee is charged when both sleeping units are not tents. Each site posts its own maximum number of people.

'Reservations are accepted up to five months in advance', released 7am ET. Maximum stay is the longest in the registry: 'The maximum stay on a campsite at all other parks and during off-season is twenty-three consecutive nights', reduced to 7-14 nights in peak season (July 1 to Labour Day Saturday) at the busiest parks such as Algonquin and Pinery - so max_stay_nights holds the off-season figure and a July booking should assume less. fees.note: Online reservation fee $9.74 + HST = $11.00 per reservation ($13.00 by phone or at a park), 2026-27 ('Fees effective from April 1, 2026 to March 31, 2027'); change and cancellation fees from $8.50 online. See the BC row's note on Canadian rating.price_tier. A second vehicle on a campsite pays the additional-vehicle fee, C$12.50 / C$11.00 / C$9.00 a day before HST at fee levels A / B / C (Ontario residents 65+ C$10.20 / C$9.00 / C$7.40), April 1, 2026 to March 31, 2027 (ontarioparks.ca/fees/additionalvehicle/2026, read 2026-11-07). Add-ons (2026-11-07): Posted camping and additional-vehicle fees are before 13% HST (a Fee Level A non-electrical site is $42.00 + $5.46 HST = $47.46); the $11 online reservation fee already includes HST. The campsite permit includes parking for one vehicle, so a camper pays no daily vehicle permit for it; each further vehicle needs an additional vehicle permit (per day, by fee level) and may have to park away from the site; the park caps how many. No more than six people on a campsite unless they are a single family of parents and their children. At most one piece of shelter equipment may be a trailer or motorhome. The fee tables show Regular, Ontario Senior and Ontario Persons with Disabilities rates only; no weekend or holiday premium is posted.

booking.note: Reservations are mandatory - 'Campers must make a reservation before setting up on any site' - but same-day booking is allowed: 'Camping reservations are required and can be made on the same day of your arrival or up to 11 months before your planned occupancy date.' No clock time is published, so reserve_until holds end-of-day. THE 2-NIGHT MINIMUM KEYS ON WHEN YOU BOOK, NOT WHEN YOU STAY, which no other agency here does: 'reservations booked before May 15 for stays between May 15 and Oct. 31 require a minimum 2-night reservation', while sites still available after May 15 may be booked for one night. So it never binds a late booker, and a one-night search must NOT exclude Wisconsin on the strength of it. Holiday weekends need 3 nights. Remote forest areas may have non-reservable camping; standard park sites do not.

fees.note: 'Nonresident campers will pay $15 per night in addition to the standard campsite fee' - THE LARGEST per-night non-resident surcharge in the registry, three times New York's $5 and roughly double Virginia's worst case. On a four-night stay that is $60 before the campsite is paid for. A vehicle admission pass is required on top (daily, or a 12-month pass); resident/non-resident amounts for the pass were not published on the page checked. Add-ons (2026-11-07): Vehicle admission (rates effective Aug. 19, 2025): daily $13 Wisconsin plates, $16 out-of-state, $3 Wisconsin residents 65+; 12-month $28 / $50 ($13 for residents 65+). A camper without a 12-month pass buys one daily pass for each night of camping. A vehicle towed or carried in and not driven on the property gets a free towed-vehicle pass; any other second vehicle needs its own admission pass. The rule fee schedule (NR 45.12(2)) says camping fees include state sales tax; county sales tax is not mentioned. Statute allows a $1 Friday-Sunday-night fee and waterview (up to $5) and market (+$3) premiums at named campgrounds, but site prices are shown per site at booking and no flat weekend premium on every park was confirmed.

booking.note: THE CLEANEST HANDOFF IN THE REGISTRY, and the model the others should be read against: 'Campers can book a same-day reservation until 2 p.m. on their intended day of arrival' and 'First come, first served camping is still available for unreserved sites after 2:30 p.m.' Two mechanisms with a published boundary and a half-hour of slack between them, effective 2025-03-24 when same-day booking expanded from a few parks to all reservable campgrounds. Reservable season is May 15 - Sept 15 at most parks, some year-round or wider; outside it, and in winter when loops close, sites may be first-come anyway. From 2025-08-19 a reservation cannot exceed 10 nights, nor push the camper past a 90-night annual total - max_stay_nights holds the per-reservation cap, not the annual one.

fees.note: Camping includes parking for one vehicle: the $10 day / $45 annual Discover Pass is not needed in the park you are camping in. The $8 reservation fee is per reservation online ($10 by phone); people who do not live in Washington pay a $15 fee per reservation on top of it, so a first-come stay pays neither. Statewide ranges: peak season (May 15 - Sept. 15) standard sites $31-43, partial utility $41-51, full utility $46-56; shoulder season (April 1 - May 14, Sept. 16 - Oct. 31) $23-35 / $35-46 / $41-51, running through the winter at Cape Disappointment, Grayland Beach, Pacific Beach and Fort Worden; winter $23 / $35 / $41; primitive sites $12 all year. Extra vehicle $10 a night. Tax included. Each park's own prices are on its entry. Add-ons (2026-11-07): Rule (WAC 352-32-030): one car and one recreational vehicle a site, plus one more vehicle without sleeping quarters where it fits; eight people overnight unless a ranger allows more. The fees page lists no per-person charge.

booking.note: 180 days for camping, a year for cabins and lodges. Walk-up is explicit and has a registration path: 'Non-reservable campsites are assigned on a first-come, first-served basis' and 'first-come, first-served campers must register at the entrance booth or office, or at a self-registration drop box' - the same honour-system shape as Pennsylvania. fcfs is 'some_sites' rather than 'always' because the wording covers NON-RESERVABLE sites specifically and does not say unbooked reservable ones may be taken. No minimum stay for standard sites (cabins need two nights). No same-day cutoff published.

fees.note: 'A Motor Vehicle Park Entry Permit is required on all licensed vehicles entering any state park, state recreation area or state historical park.' Daily permit $7 for a Nebraska-licensed vehicle, $14 for any other (annual $35 / $70; a duplicate for a second household vehicle half price). The $8.50 reservation fee is on each online booking; first-come sites have none. Campsite prices are statewide by site level (camping rates grid) and are on the entries. Add-ons (2026-11-07): A daily park entry permit runs until noon the day after activation, so one covers one night. Every vehicle needs its own permit; a site holds one camping unit with one tent (or two tents) and one tow or towed vehicle, and extra vehicles park in designated lots. Up to 8 people a site unless the superintendent allows more; additional tents or occupants may be charged an additional camping fee. Tax is added on top of the posted rates and on the reservation fee: state and local sales tax on RV sites plus lodging tax (tent-only sites pay lodging tax only), so the rate varies by location. The reservation fee is per unit reserved, non-refundable. Lake McConaughy and Lake Ogallala charge $5 more Thursday-Saturday in season (on those entries).

booking.note: 'Reservations are not required for campsites, but are highly recommended' - one of the few agencies left where turning up is a supported way to camp rather than a fallback, and seven parks run self-registration envelope stations for exactly that (Bear Butte, Burke Lake, Little Moreau, North Wheeler, Okobojo Point and all Lakeside Use Areas). The recommendation is not idle: 'For summer weekend stays, most campsites and cabins are reserved within a week of reservations opening', so fcfs 'always' describes the policy, not the odds. WINDOW: 90 days, released at 7 a.m. CT / 6 a.m. MT on the first day, EXCEPT CUSTER STATE PARK, which takes reservations ONE YEAR ahead - the seven Custer campgrounds carry that on their own entries. FOUR PARKS CANNOT BE RESERVED AT ALL: gfp.sd.gov/first-come lists Bear Butte, Burke Lake, Little Moreau and Okobojo Point as non-reservable, 'Campers must be at the park to reserve the campsite. Camping units must be left on-site at time of registration.' The camp page's own first-come accordion lists three more (Lake Hiddenwood, Lake Louise, North Wheeler) but their park pages say 'Make reservation online or call' - the two pages disagree, so only the four appear on entries. SAME-DAY booking is not statewide: it exists at exactly two campgrounds, Yankton at Lewis and Clark and Center Lake at Custer, from 7 a.m. CT / 6 a.m. MT on the arrival day, and the unit must be ON the site by 10 p.m. or the rest of the reservation is forfeited. reserve_until is therefore absent rather than a statewide cutoff. NO MINIMUM STAY is published anywhere - none on the camp, campsite, regulation or fee pages - so absent here means looked-for and not found. max_stay_nights is 'the maximum number of consecutive nights that a camper may stay at any one state park area is 14'. CHECK-IN AND CHECK-OUT ARE BOTH 4 P.M. (Custer: noon and noon), which is a full 24-hour site and unlike any other agency in this registry - an afternoon arrival costs no part of the night before. Occupancy is capped at 6 people and ONE camping unit per site: 'If two camping units share a site, each unit must pay the camping fee.' Cancelling within 7 days of arrival costs half a night (30 days for cabins, lodges and Custer's French Creek Horse Camp), and 'cancellations to the beginning of a reservation are not allowed' - you cannot trim the front of a stay, only cancel it.

fees.note: Two statewide camping tiers, the same price for everyone: Statewide Basic $16, Statewide Modern $23, plus a flat $7 Electrical Fee on an electric site. Custer State Park is its own tier ($27 modern, $37 equestrian) and its campgrounds carry that on their entries. Each park publishes its own pair on its gfp.sd.gov page, which is where the entry-level figures come from. SOUTH DAKOTA'S NON-RESIDENT CHARGE IS A BOOKING FEE, NOT A RATE: 'A $10 per site, non-refundable reservation fee applies to non-residents' - so it lands ONCE per site reservation however many nights, which is why `per` is stay. reservation_fee 0 is a real zero: a resident booking online pays nothing to reserve ('Save money by making your reservation online'). Phone booking costs $6 resident / $16 non-resident. THE ENTRANCE LICENCE IS THE CHARGE PEOPLE FORGET - 'Camping fees do not include entrance fees, which are required year-round', it is per VEHICLE not per site, and a daily licence issued to a registered camper runs to 4 p.m. the following day, so one covers one night. Daily $10 resident / $15 non-resident; annual $40 / $60; double (two vehicles) $60 / $90; a resident-only transferable licence $90; motorcycles the same as cars, as a handlebar wristband. CUSTER IS SEPARATE AND BUYING IN THE WRONG ORDER COSTS MONEY: the daily licence is 'not available for purchase at Custer State Park' and Custer's $25 seven-day, per-vehicle licence is 'not available for purchase outside of Custer State Park', though an annual licence is valid in both. For a non-resident a week at Custer is $25 against the $60 annual, but add two daily licences elsewhere at $15 and the annual wins. None of them is valid on the George S. Mickelson Trail, which sells its own ($20 annual / $5 daily) - worth knowing in the Black Hills, where the trail runs past several of these campgrounds. Firewood $6.72 a bundle; out-of-state firewood is banned. Add-ons (2026-11-07): ARSD confirms the figures (rules amended Nov 11, 2024). A site holds one camper unit: a family, or a party of six or fewer; the manager may let two units (12 people at most) share a site at twice the camping fee. Camping fees are per camper unit, with no per-person charge outside Custer's French Creek natural area and group camps. Each vehicle needs its own entrance licence.

season.note: 'Camping is welcome year-round in most parks', which is unusual this far north and is the agency default rather than a promise about a given park - a few close for eagle nesting. What closes everywhere is the plumbing: 'Between Oct. 1 and April 30, showers, flush toilets and other water systems may be closed... Vault toilets usually remain open.' So an off-season night is a dry-camping night, and the electric may still be on. Each park page states its own 'Open:' line.

discounts.note: The military discount is real but NARROW, and it is residency-gated like everything else here: 'South Dakota State Parks offers lifetime state park entrance licenses for disabled veterans who are residents of South Dakota and are deemed 100% disabled. Approved applicants will also receive a 50% discount on camping fees' (also POW and Purple Heart recipients). An out-of-state veteran gets nothing; past and present military can apply for free entrance only when attending an approved military-group event. SENIORS GET NOTHING, and GFP says so in as many words: 'No, there is not a senior discount for park entrance or camping fees.' The only other break is Go Fourth, a free daily or discounted annual entrance licence for South Dakota fourth-graders.

booking.note: Verbatim on 19 of the 23 park camping pages: 'Reservations may be made for no less than two consecutive nights on weekends (Friday and Saturday) or one night Sunday through Thursday' - so the pair Friday+Saturday triggers it, unlike PA where Saturday alone does. NOT universal, and the exceptions run both ways: Lost River says 'Reservations may be made any night' (no minimum at all), while Camp Creek applies it only 'during the season on weekends starting on the Thursday before Memorial Day and ends the day after Labor Day'. The rule here is the majority default; a one-night weekend booking is worth checking on the park's own page. max_stay_nights is from the legislative rule (58CSR32 s2.4): 'The rental period for any campsite may not exceed 14 consecutive nights' - 'except that, after Labor Day until May 1st of the following year, the area superintendent, at his or her discretion, may rent campsites for longer periods when vacant campsites are available.' WINDOW UNRESOLVED: no official page publishes how far ahead booking opens. Every park page says only 'Campsites may be reserved anytime online, by phone, or at the campground office', rates and the calendar live inside the Inntopia booking engine, and the 12-months figure in circulation is a third-party aggregator's - window_opens_days is absent rather than guessed. FCFS NOT CONFIRMED: no campsite on any of the 23 pages is offered first-come (the only 'first-come' text found anywhere is Stonewall's boat MOORING POSTS), and two parks say the opposite - Seneca: 'Before occupying any campsite, campers must have a paid reservation and all sites are reservable', Tygart: 'All campsites are reservable.' Against that, 58CSR32 s2.1 still contemplates paying 'in person at the campground check-in station or park office'. Beware the pre-online park brochures and campground applications still served from wvstateparks.com: they describe held-back FCFS sites and say reservations 'must be made at least two (2) days prior to arrival', which the current system contradicts. Check-in 1 p.m., check-out noon; s2.6 'Campsites shall be vacated by 12:00 noon'. Cancellation: 'Reservations canceled at least 60 days prior to arrival may request a refund for the deposit paid', credit-only inside 60 days, nothing inside 7.

fees.note: NO RATES PUBLISHED. Scanned all 23 park camping pages: not one dollar figure appears on any of them, and there is no statewide camping-rates page - the numbers exist only inside the booking engine (book.wvstateparks.com, Inntopia), per park and per site type. nightly_low/high are absent rather than sampled from one park. NON-RESIDENT RATE: none found on any official page, so nonresident is absent, not zero. The only residency-linked term West Virginia publishes is a discount, not a surcharge: 58CSR32 s2.13, 'West Virginia residents who are totally and permanently disabled are entitled to a 50 percent discount on campground rental fees from the day after Labor Day until four days prior to Memorial Day only', on application for a permanent campground discount card. Reservation/transaction fee not published either; full payment is taken at booking. Add-ons (2026-11-07): No entrance fee anywhere in the state park system. At most two motor vehicles and one camping unit per campsite (58CSR32 s2.5), so a motorhome towing a car fills the limit. The site fee covers no other fee-charged facility. The booking site adds taxes and fees to online reservations (stated for lodge rooms); the amounts for campsites are not published.

booking.note: Verbatim: 'Reservations can be made up to 13 months in advance. Georgia residents may make reservations up to 14 months in advance.' window_opens_days is the 13 months every traveller gets (395 days); GA residents get 425. That RESIDENT-ADVANTAGE WINDOW is the first one found in any agency checked - elsewhere residency changes the price, not the queue. Cutoff: 'Campsites can be reserved until 4:00pm on the day of arrival. All other facilities can be reserved up to 7:00am on day of arrival' - so 16:00 is the CAMPSITE figure and the cabin/yurt one is earlier, not later. Minimum stay: 'A two-night minimum is required for weekend reservations, and a three-night minimum is required for Memorial Day, Labor Day and Independence Day weekends' - the same weekend+holiday pair as every other state verified, but note the holiday list is THREE summer weekends and excludes Thanksgiving, which DOES carry the 3-night rule for cottages. No booking-window waiver is published, so the IN/NC waived_if shape is deliberately absent; the relief is a different shape entirely - 'Walk-ins may occupy a site for just one night', i.e. the minimum binds RESERVATIONS, not arrivals. fcfs is 'after_cutoff' for that reason: unlike NC, Georgia designates no walk-up-only sites, so what exists after 4pm is an unreserved site you take on arrival. One park publishes an actual self-registration lock box - Watson Mill Bridge, December-February, when the office and main campground are closed and only equestrian sites, stalls and log cabins are available first-come. max_stay_nights is 14 CONSECUTIVE days at any one park, then 'must vacate the park for at least three nights before returning'. DO NOT confuse that with Georgia's WMA rule (391-4-2-.61: 14 days then SEVEN days out, plus a one-mile radius clause) - a search for the state-park limit hands back the WMA one, and three of this database's GA entries really are wildlife-division sites. Check-in 1pm-10pm, check-out before noon, and most park gates lock at 10pm, which matters more than the cutoff for a late arrival. Four LODGE parks - Amicalola Falls, Georgia Veterans, Little Ocmulgee, Unicoi - are run by Coral Hospitality / the North Georgia Mountain Authority, which the agency says handle 'their reservations and policies' themselves.

fees.note: Rates are published as a RANGE and hedged: 'In most cases, rates are $23 to $50 for regular campsites'. That range spans site types - Georgia publishes no base-vs-hookup breakdown anywhere on its own site, so no `surcharges` can be derived and nightly_high is not a plain-site figure. Measured negative: not one of the 42 park pages scraped carries a camping rate; the only dollar figures on them are historic-site admission, museum admission and Don Carter's $15 equestrian trail fee. ParkPass is the charge a camper actually forgets: $10 per vehicle per day, 'required for all vehicles', NOT included in the reservation - but 'Overnight customers pay the daily Park Pass fee only once during their stay', which is why per is vehicle_stay rather than vehicle_day. An annual pass is $70 (50% off for seniors 62+, 25% for active military and veterans, in person only), so it pays for itself on the eighth park day of a year. The pass is NOT valid at Jekyll Island, Stone Mountain, Corps of Engineers lakes, Lake Lanier, or at WMAs and Public Fishing Areas (those need a Lands Pass) - all of which this database holds GA entries for. No separate reservation/booking fee is charged and none is published, and there is no non-resident camping rate: residency in Georgia buys an earlier booking window instead (see booking.note). Cancellation, campsites: one change free, then a $10 transfer fee; cancelling 8+ days out costs $10; 7 or fewer days out forfeits 50% of the use fee. A no-show - not checked in by noon the day AFTER arrival - is treated as a cancellation, forfeits 50%, and releases the rest of the nights. Deposit: 50% at booking 15+ days out, 100% within 14 days. 'We do not charge a separate cleaning fee' for any accommodation. Add-ons (2026-11-07): The ParkPass is $10 a vehicle, paid once for an overnight stay, and is not part of the reservation; every vehicle needs one, so a towed car pays its own. The annual ParkPass is $70. Six people per campsite at most; one motor home, two more cars and one tent.

discounts.note: Both discounts here are real but NARROWER than the flag suggests, so read the terms before quoting either. Military: 'Disabled veterans who are Georgia residents AND present a Certificate of Eligibility card are entitled to a 25% discount on individual accommodations' (O.C.G.A. 12-3-9.1) - Georgia residency AND a disability certificate, and it is REIMBURSED AT CHECK-IN rather than taken off the online price. An out-of-state veteran gets nothing on the campsite; the only general military discount is 25% off the $70 annual ParkPass. Seniors 62+ get 20% off campsite rates year-round, one campsite per senior, not valid for group camping, and only 'when reservation is registered to a senior' - that is an AGENCY discount, not the America the Beautiful pass, which is why interagency_senior_access is absent rather than true. Friends of Georgia State Parks membership also discounts camping.

booking.note: Verbatim: 'You can reserve a site any time between one day and 4 months before your arrival date.' The window is CALENDAR-MONTH arithmetic, not a day count - DCR's own worked example is 'if you're dreaming of pitching your tent under the stars on August 12, set your alarm for April 12' - so window_opens_days 120 is the approximation and the real opening is the same day-of-month four months out. The front of the season is not rolling at all: 2026 reservations ALL opened at once, 'Wednesday, February 18, 2026 at 9 a.m. EST sharp'. CUTOFF: the reservation page's 'one day' is contradicted by DCR's own newer season page, which is the specific one - 'Walk-in camping might be off the table, but you can still seize the day with same-day reservations until 2 p.m. EST through Reserve America' - hence reserve_until 14:00 on the arrival date. fcfs is 'never' and DCR says so flatly: 'Walk-in camping will not be permitted. Reservations are required.' MINIMUM STAY, PUBLISHED BUT NOT OBSERVED: 'There is a 2-day minimum stay at most campsites' - no weekend or holiday scoping, unlike every other state verified so far, and 'most' is doing real work. FIRSTHAND (AWH): trip 16 booked two separate SINGLE nights at Loraine Campground, Harold Parker State Forest, in August 2023 - Saturday 8/12 and Friday 8/18, both weekend nights - and the identical 2-day-minimum sentence was live on mass.gov that month (Wayback, 2023-07-06 onward). So this is a default to check per park, never a bar on a one-night search (doc 2.2). max_stay_nights is 14 CUMULATIVE days 'in any one campground between Memorial Day and Labor Day' - a seasonal total rather than a consecutive-nights cap, so two week-long stays at the same park in one summer exhaust it. Check-in 1 p.m.-9 p.m., check-out before 11 a.m., quiet hours 10 p.m.-7 a.m., generators banned during them except for medical use. A reserved site is held only until 8:00 a.m. the day AFTER arrival, then no-showed with no refund. Most campgrounds cap a site at 2 tents (or 1 tent + 1 trailer/RV), 2 vehicles and 4 adults, and a dog needs a physical rabies certificate at check-in - 'This is required for the safety of all campers and pets - no exceptions.' For the 2026 season DCR allows NO VISITORS at all: 'Sorry, no visitors allowed, but feel free to gather in our awesome day use areas.' Changes and cancellations cost $10 each; a day-of-arrival cancellation must be phoned to the campground and forfeits the first night's fee on top. A reservation whose departure date falls outside the 4-month window cannot be changed or cancelled until 18 days after it was made.

fees.note: Massachusetts publishes a rate table naming EVERY campground, so the exact pair is written on each entry (doc 3) and this row carries the shape. Four tiers, MA resident / out-of-state: coastal $22-24 / $70, inland $17 / $54, limited-service $14 / $40, primitive $8 / $20. nightly_low/high span the drive-in tiers this database holds; the $8 primitive tier is hike-in and boat-in sites. THE NON-RESIDENT RATE IS THE FACT ABOUT MASSACHUSETTS: about 3.2x the resident rate ($17 -> $54, $22 -> $70; 2.9x on the $24 and $14 tiers), by far the largest differential of any agency in this registry, and it is the CAMPING rate rather than a gate fee, so no pass avoids it. AWH's own note on Loraine Campground - 'High surcharge for out-of-state' - predates this row. Per-night add-ons on top: electric $6 (Harold Parker, Horseneck, Salisbury, Scusset), water $4 (Salisbury, Scusset). An unexplained 'Trust Surcharge' of $2-$5 is charged at four coastal campgrounds (Scusset $2, Salisbury $3, Nickerson and Wellfleet Hollow $5, the latter two non-MA residents only) - the asterisk marking it has NO footnote anywhere on the fee page. Booking costs a $4.50 non-refundable transaction charge PER RESERVATION, which is a real per-night cost on a one-night booking. ENTRANCE is absent rather than zero: no entrance fee is charged for camping, but DCR does charge DAY-USE PARKING at the same parks (2026: $8 MA / $30 non-MA at most, $14 / $40 at Salisbury and Scusset, collected May 23 - Oct 12), the $60 annual MassParks pass and the $10 lifetime senior pass are MA-plate only, and the pass is explicitly 'not valid for camping' - whether a camper's extra vehicle pays the day-use rate is not published. Other tiers, resident / out-of-state: group sites $35 / $100 up to 25 people plus $1 per person over; cabins $50-$75 / $130-$170; yurts $45-$55 / $120-$140. Add-ons (2026-11-07): The Commonwealth's fee regulation (801 CMR 4.02) prices DCR camping per site per day and lists no extra-person or extra-vehicle charge, nor any weekend or holiday rate; its only parking row under camping is day-visitor parking ($8 a vehicle a day). Most campgrounds allow 2 vehicles and 4 adults (or 2 adults and the children in their care) a site; Scusset RV sites take one camping vehicle only. The regulation's inland non-resident figure ($55) is a dollar above the current fee page's $54. Tax: no source states whether the room occupancy excise applies to a DCR campsite.

season.note: Per park and published as exact dates for the coming year, so opens/closes are written on the ENTRIES from DCR's own schedule rather than generalized here. 2026 shape: campgrounds open 4/9 (Horseneck, Scusset) through 6/17 (Peddocks Island), most of the inland forests on 5/7 or 5/14, and the last night ranges from 9/6 (Erving, Otter River, Willard Brook, Granville, Mt. Greylock) through 10/11 for most, to 11/21-11/28 at the beaches. Several parks run a weekend-only shoulder - Salisbury is Thu/Fri/Sat only from 10/22, Harold Parker Thu-Sun from 10/15 - and Granville is Fri/Sat/Sun ALL season. NOT year-round anywhere: no DCR campground stays open through the winter, unlike the neighbouring states. Dates shift by a few days each year, so re-read the schedule page each spring; the 2026 one is dated March 2, 2026.

discounts.note: NO CAMPING DISCOUNT FOUND, and that is a measured negative rather than an unchecked field: the fee table, the reservation page, the campground regulations page and the 2026 season page carry no senior, military, veteran or disability camping rate. What Massachusetts discounts is PARKING, and only for its own residents - a $10 lifetime Senior Parking Pass for MA residents 62+ and the $60 annual pass, both verified by MA plate or MA licence, and both 'not valid for camping'. The residency lever here works the other way round (see fees.note).

booking.note: Missouri State Parks (DNR). Reservations open 'at 7 a.m. CT 12 months prior to the first day of your trip' (the same 12 months is on 39 of the 40 park camping pages read) and can be made 'up to 7 p.m. the day of arrival', online or at 877-422-6766. 39 parks and historic sites take reservations, and each 'allows all campsites to be reserved during their reservable season'; 'Campsites that are not reserved remain available for walk-up registration' (36 of the 40 park pages say the same), so fcfs is after_cutoff: there are no walk-up-only loops. Exceptions: Battle of Athens is reservable only Apr 15-Oct 31 and walk-up only otherwise, Graham Cave is all first-come November-March, and Watkins Mill keeps sites 1-34, 98 and 99 walk-in only in the off-season; Prairie and Taum Sauk Mountain are not on the reservation list. No agency-wide minimum stay: 'A two-night minimum stay on the weekend (Friday and Saturday or Saturday and Sunday) is required at Big Lake, Lake of the Ozarks, St. Joe, Mark Twain, Wakonda, Wallace and Watkins Mill state parks' - those seven entries carry it themselves - and Bennett Spring's page says it has 'no minimum stay requirement'. max_stay_nights: 'Camping is limited to any 15 days within a 30-consecutive-day period at any one park.' Check-in 3 p.m., checkout 2 p.m.; a site not claimed within the first 24 hours of the stay (3 p.m. to 3 p.m.) is resold. Changes until 7 p.m. the day before arrival ($5.25); cancelling 1-30 days out costs $10 plus the reservation fee, 31 or more days out only the reservation fee.

fees.note: Base (basic-site) rates from the 2026 rate charts: $15 a night in the on-season at most parks ($16 at Long Branch, Roaring River, Table Rock and Lake Wappapello's Asher Creek loop) and $14 in the off-season. The on-season runs Apr 1-Oct 31, from Feb 25 at Roaring River, Bennett Spring and Montauk, from Apr 15 at some northern parks, and March-November at Table Rock. Nine 'value camping' parks charge less on weeknights (Graham Cave, Lake Wappapello, Pomme de Terre, Robertsville, Stockton, Truman, Mark Twain, Van Meter and Washington), so the range runs from $8 (Stockton, off-season) to $17 (Truman's holiday weekends). Hookup sites at most parks, on-season: 30-amp electric $27, 50-amp $29, electric/water 50-amp $32, sewer/electric/water 50-amp $35 (off-season $23/$25/$26/$29); 'Camping rates are charged on the basis of available utilities, whether used or not.' Advance reservations add a nonrefundable fee per site: $6.50 online, $8 by phone. Each of the 40 park entries carries its own 2026 figures, surcharges and reservation fee; they are not row fields here because the conservation-area row inherits this one field by field. No non-resident rate: one price list for everyone. No entrance fee: 'admission to all Missouri state parks and historic sites is free' (DNR news release, May 18, 2026). Add-ons (2026-11-07): Reservation fee $6.50 online, $8 through the call center, per site; change $5.25 online, cancellation $10 plus the reservation fee. (The reservation fee can sit on the row: the conservation-area row names its own ref and no longer inherits this one.) Posted camping rates include sales tax. Typical site capacity is two sleeping units (one wheeled), two other vehicles and six people, doubled at family sites; exceeding the site's design may bring extra fees (St. Joe charges $5 a night per vehicle past two). Holiday-weekend and value-camping rates are per park.

The America the Beautiful Senior Pass is NOT accepted as proof of age ('issued at age 62 ... please provide proof other than these two federal passes'), while the Access Pass IS accepted as proof of disability - so interagency_senior_access stays absent: either way the discount is Missouri's own $2, not a federal one.

Be sure to have a backup plan in case the spot where you want to camp is already occupied.' 'Most', because 'Some areas require a special use permit for all camping' and some allow camping only in designated sites - read the area's own page - and 'some areas expand or restrict camping during firearm hunting seasons'. The Wildlife Code (3 CSR 10-11.140) limits a stay to 'fourteen (14) consecutive days in any thirty- (30-) day period' and each camper to 30 camping days a calendar year on all department land; two camping or sleeping units per established site (one at Thomas Hill Reservoir); quiet hours 10 p.m.-6 a.m., with visitors out of the campground by 10 p.m.; groups of more than ten need a special use permit.

fees.note: 'All camping on conservation areas is free.' Little is provided for it: 'no RV hookups are provided at any department area. Campers should expect to bring their own water.' Designated campgrounds may have fire rings, tables, dumpsters and latrines, but most conservation-area camping is primitive. Add-ons (2026-11-07): No charge to enter a conservation area, and camping is free for everyone, so no non-resident, extra-person or extra-vehicle charge. Most camping is first come, first served; some areas require a special use permit for all camping, and groups of more than 10 need one. Only two camping or sleeping units a site where sites are established.

booking.note: Oregon State Parks on ReserveAmerica, or 800-452-5687. 'New reservations are accepted starting the same day as arrival through six months in advance. New sites come online at 6 a.m. daily' (on 2026-10-20 the site read 'Now accepting reservations for arrival October 20, 2026 to April 19, 2027', so window_opens_days carries 180). Same-day online booking has been statewide since 2024-01-01, so there is no cutoff: 'At campgrounds that accept reservations, any available sites can be booked the same day through an online reservation, which can be made from home or at the park via a digital device or a park ranger' - turning up works wherever a site is free, which is why fcfs is always. 'Reservations are not required to camp' anywhere. Campgrounds that take no reservations use a booth or self-registration envelopes; OPRD lists Jackson Kimball, Goose Lake, Bates, Cascara (Fall Creek), Catherine Creek, Hilgard Junction, Jasper Point (Prineville Reservoir), Minam, Red Bridge and Ukiah-Dale, plus Cottonwood Canyon November-March and mixed walk-up loops at The Cove Palisades (spring and fall), Emigrant Springs, Farewell Bend and Lake Owyhee (all reservable in summer); those entries say first-come themselves. STAY LIMIT (OAR 736-010-0020): 'The maximum length of stay for campers is 14 consecutive nights in a 17 night span. After three nights out of the park, campers may return to start a new stay.' No minimum stay is published. Eight people and one RV per site (OAR 736-010-0050); quiet hours 10 p.m.-7 a.m.; 'All vehicles, including towed vehicles, must be able to fit into the paved driveway space' (driveway lengths are on ReserveAmerica). Cancel online or by phone up to the day before arrival (on the day, call the park); changes and cancellations carry a transaction fee.

fees.note: Each entry carries its own 2026 price. OPRD's rate ranges, effective May 1, 2026, tax included (resident, peak): full hookup $30-42, electric with water $28-40, tent $20-27, primitive $0-15, extra vehicle $10. 'Oregon Parks and Recreation Department charges out-of-state residents 25% more' (full hookup $38-53 non-resident). At the 29 busiest parks the rate is the top of the range May 1-September 30 and on every Friday, Saturday and Sunday night; from October 1 to April 30 weekdays are cheaper than weekends. The $10 reservation fee is per site, by phone or online, 'unless it's a same-day reservation, in which case the $10 fee is waived'. No entrance fee for campers: a registered camper displaying the overnight receipt is exempt from the day-use parking permit (OAR 736-015-0030(5)(d)), which otherwise costs $5 a day or $60 ($75 out of state) for 12 months at the parks that charge it. Veterans with a service-connected disability and active-duty military on leave camp free, up to ten nights a calendar month, with no reservation deposit (OAR 736-015-0035); State Parks Day (first Saturday in June) is free for everyone. Add-ons (2026-11-07): A camper needs no day-use parking permit (display the camping receipt). The permit now costs $10 a day ($12 non-resident) or $60 ($75) for 12 months, replacing the $5 figure above. One car or truck may be towed in free; a second vehicle driven in pays the $10 extra-vehicle fee on site. Eight people a site usually, six at some sites. The overnight-rental rule (OAR 736-015-0020) has no per-person charge for individual sites, only hiker/biker per-person rates. Rates include lodging tax.

booking.note: Manitoba Parks Reservation Service (goingtocamp), or 1-888-482-2267 (204-948-3333 in Winnipeg). There is no rolling window: 'Camping inventory becomes available for reservations in April', on staged launch days at 7 a.m. (2026: cabins, yurts and group areas April 13; Birds Hill, Winnipeg Beach and Grand Beach April 14; Whiteshell April 15; Northern and Western regions April 16; everything else April 17), and from then the whole season is bookable. Each campground's reservable dates are on Manitoba's Operating Dates list: many stop taking reservations days or weeks before they close (Beresford Lake reserves to Sept 6 but stays open to Oct 12), after which every site is first-come, and a campground with no reservation dates there takes none. 'All reservable sites can now be booked up to 3:00 p.m. on the day of arrival.' 'Although reservations are recommended, some campsites are available on a first-come, first-served basis.' MINIMUM STAY: two nights over long weekends, including the Saturday and Sunday nights (2026: Victoria Day, Terry Fox Day, Labour Day, Thanksgiving); three nights Thursday-Sunday at Birds Hill during the Winnipeg Folk Festival; and a few designated sites carry a seven-night minimum in July and August (Bakers Narrows Bay 2 sites 41-46; Birds Hill Chipping Bay 1-10 and Savannah Bay 1-10; Falcon Beach J 1-10 and Y1 1-10; St. Malo Bay 2 1-10) - every other site books for one night. MAXIMUM STAY: 21 nights on one reservation, and no one may 'occupy the same campsite for more than 21 consecutive nights'. Check-in 4 p.m., check-out 3 p.m.; a late arrival is held until 11 a.m. the next day. Six people or one family per site, one camping unit (plus a tent if space allows); quiet time 11 p.m.-9 a.m. Cancelling 4 or more days ahead costs $10 plus the reservation fee; within 3 days, the first night as well.

fees.note: Camping fees are per entry; most carry their own 2026 rate. The $10 reservation fee is per booking and non-refundable. Every vehicle needs a provincial park vehicle permit, GST included: $9.50 a day (to midnight), $16.50 for three consecutive days, $44.50 for the year (to April 30, 2027; up to two plates on one permit); bought at manitobaelicensing.ca, a park office or a retailer, the same price for residents and visitors. Permits are not needed on the 2026 free-entry weekends (Family Fishing Weekend June 12-14, Parks Week July 13-19, Labour Day weekend September 4-7) or in February 2027, but camping fees still apply. A Manitoba permit is not valid in Riding Mountain National Park. Add-ons (2026-11-07): Campers need a park vehicle permit on top of the camping fee (the daily permit runs to midnight on the day bought, so a one-night stay touches two days; the three-day permit is $16.50). The Park Fees Regulation sets every fee, GST included: one nightly fee per campsite, with no non-resident, per-person or extra-vehicle charge and no weekend or holiday premium (campgrounds run by private operators set their own). The $10 reservation fee is per stay and facility, online or by phone; changes $4. Six people or one family per site (parents and children under 18, a grandparent allowed); one camping unit, and one vehicle per campsite unless an officer approves more, guests parking in designated areas. Every vehicle needs its own permit; an annual permit can carry two plates.

booking.note: Sask Parks reservation system (parks.saskatchewan.ca) or the call centre, 1-833-775-7275, or by calling the park. There is no rolling window: nightly sites for the whole season (May 14-September 30 in 2026) open on staggered launch days at 7 a.m. CST (2026: April 14 Candle Lake, Good Spirit Lake, Lac La Ronge, Meadow Lake, Rowan's Ravine, Saskatchewan Landing; April 15 Blackstrap, Bronson Forest, Buffalo Pound, Duck Mountain, Moose Mountain, Porcupine Hills; April 16 Crooked Lake, Cypress Hills, Danielson, Great Blue Heron, Greenwater Lake, The Battlefords; April 17 Douglas, Echo Valley, Fort Carlton, Makwa Lake, Narrow Hills, Pike Lake). 'Same-day bookings are allowed until 11 p.m. CST on the day of arrival.' Spring camping before the season cannot be reserved online. NO STAY LIMIT: 'Campers can book nightly camping for as long as they would like on the same campsite provided there is availability', and no minimum stay for campsites (yurts only). Seasonal sites unsold by May 14 become nightly sites. Check-in after 2 p.m., out by noon CST; a site is held 24 hours past check-in, and a no-show can cost up to four nights. Change and cancellation fees depend on the site type and come on top of the non-refundable reservation fee. Several northern campgrounds and the recreation sites are self-registration only; those entries say first-come.

fees.note: Each entry carries its own 2026 price; Sask Parks' 2026 nightly rates (May 14-September 30), taxes included: full service $49, electric $35, non-electric $20, economy $18, the same every night. The $12 reservation fee is per campsite, plus $2 through the call centre, non-refundable. Every vehicle in a provincial park needs an entry permit ($11 a day, $42 a week, $82 a year; free for Saskatchewan residents 65 and older), carried on the entries that need it; the recreation sites charge none. Add-ons (2026-11-07): Every vehicle in a provincial park needs a park entry permit, charged on top of camping: $11 a day, $42 a week, $82 a year ($45 for an annual bought October 1 to April 30), the same for everyone; free for Saskatchewan residents 65+ and for First Nations, Metis and Inuit people exercising traditional use rights, 25% off with a SaskAbilities accessible parking permit. There is no extra-vehicle camping fee, but a towed car needs its own entry permit. Sask Parks' complete 2026-27 rates and fees table lists no non-resident, extra-person, extra-vehicle, weekend or holiday charge, and its fees include all applicable taxes. Reservation fee $12 online or in park, $14 through the call centre; change and cancellation $15 ($17 by phone).

booking.note: Oklahoma State Parks on ReserveAmerica (okstateparks.reserveamerica.com, linked from travelok.com/state-parks). OAC 725:30-12-5: 'Individual camping reservations are accepted up to eleven (11) months in advance' (window_opens_days carries 335). 'All sites must be reserved prior to occupancy. No sites within the parks system are available on a first-come basis', and TravelOK repeats 'Online reservations must be made for all RV and tent campsites'; a few entries name tent areas a park still runs first-come. MINIMUM STAY: 'The minimum reservation shall be for two (2) nights on weekends and three (3) nights on holiday periods'; 'at the discretion of the Manager, single night reservations may be accepted less than thirty (30) days prior to arrival' - a discretion, not a waiver, so it is not recorded as one. Check-in 5 p.m., check-out 2 p.m.; a confirmed reservation is held until 10 a.m. the day after arrival. Cancel at least five days before arrival for a full refund, or forfeit the first night. Reselling a reservation (Airbnb and the like) is illegal under 74 O.S. 2217.

fees.note: Each entry carries its own 2026 price from the booking site; Oklahoma publishes no rate table. No reservation fee was charged on the 2026 booking site (the rule permits a portal and a reservation fee); a 3% service fee applies to card payments, plus tax. 'One parking pass to this state park is included with a completed reservation'; other vehicles need their own pass for the stay. Seniors 62 and over and active or former military get 10% off the campsite base rate; 100% disabled visitors get 50% off it (utilities not discounted). A $75 card hold is taken at check-in. Add-ons (2026-11-07): A camping reservation includes one vehicle's parking pass, so the camper pays no parking fee; each further vehicle buys its own pass for the length of the stay. Only the parks that charge for parking (about two dozen of them) sell passes: TravelOK's parking-pass guide lists a one-day pass at $10 ($8 discounted rate), with three-day, week and annual options (read from a search summary, the page no longer loads).

booking.note: Montana State Parks (FWP) on ReserveAmerica, or 855-922-6768. Reservations are taken only for stays from the third Friday in May through the third Sunday in September; the rest of the year every site is first-come. 'Reservations for individual campsites ... are available up to 3 months in advance of arrival' (window_opens_days carries 90) and 'no later than one day prior to your arrival' ('There is a 1-day minimum window'); a multi-night stay booked on the first day of the window is frozen for 12 days. 'On the date of arrival, if a site is not reserved it becomes a first come first served for that night', and some parks also hold designated walk-up sites, shown as 'walk-up' on the booking map - those parks' entries say so. 20 of the 55 state parks take reservations; the fishing access sites take none (each FAS entry says first-come itself). STAY LIMIT, both: FWP's public use rules (ARM, printed on its public-use-rules page) prohibit camping 'for a period of longer than 7 nights during any consecutive 30-day period, beginning with the first night occupied unless otherwise posted by the department', and the state parks' camping policies say the same ('Campers may stay no longer than 7 nights in any thirty-day period'). No minimum stay is published on either page. Check-in 2 p.m., check-out 1 p.m. (campsites; cabins and yurts 3 p.m./noon); quiet hours 10 p.m.-7 a.m.; 8 people, one camping unit and two extra tents per site. Changes $10 (extending a stay is free); cancelling costs $10 before check-in time, plus the first night after it, and the reservation fee is never refunded; a reservation not claimed by check-in time the day after arrival is a no-show and forfeits everything.

fees.note: Each entry carries its own 2026 camping fee. STATE PARKS: 'Campsite fees range from $4-$34 per night, depending on season and available amenities'; the $10 reservation fee is per site, online or by phone, and non-refundable. Non-residents pay $10-12 a night more, which buys the day's entrance - the $50 annual Nonresident Entrance Pass or the $35 7-day pass (sold at the parks) takes that $10-12 off the camping fee instead. Day-use entrance without camping: residents free if they paid the $9 state parks fee with their vehicle registration (otherwise the non-resident fee applies), non-residents $8 a vehicle. Montana residents 62 and over, with a disability, or with veteran status get 50% off camping fees (not electric fees). FWP proposed in June 2026 to raise state-park camping fees no earlier than 2027. FISHING ACCESS SITES: no reservation and no entrance fee, but everyone 12 or older needs FWP's annual Conservation License to use one ($8 resident, $4 youth 12-17 and seniors 62+, $10 non-resident; license year from March 1; it comes with any Montana fishing license). Where camping is charged, FWP's 2026 FAS use fee table sets it statewide: $12 a night with a Montana fishing license, $18 without, $5/$7.50 for Montana residents 62 or over, disabled or veterans. Sites with no camping fee cost only the Conservation License, which those entries price for two people. Add-ons (2026-11-07): Campers owe no separate entrance fee: residents who paid the state parks fee with their vehicle registration enter free, and the non-resident camping fee already includes the non-resident's daily entrance fee. A non-resident holding the Nonresident Entrance Pass pays the resident camping fee instead. The non-resident premium is $10 a night at standard and electric sites and $8 at rustic sites. The state accommodations tax is included in the posted camping fee. A site takes up to eight people, with no per-person fee. The schedule has no weekend or holiday rate. It does have a peak season (third Friday in May to third Sunday in September) and an off-season rate, and premium campsites cost $5 more in peak season. The schedule's daily entrance authorizes one non-resident vehicle, so a second non-resident vehicle may owe its own entrance fee. No camping fee for an extra vehicle is published. Sluice Boxes and Medicine Rocks charge Montana residents no camping fee.

booking.note: Utah State Parks on ReserveAmerica, or 800-322-3770 (8 a.m.-5 p.m. Mountain, Monday-Friday). 'Individual campsites are available for reservation on a four-month rolling basis. For example, on January 10 individual sites are available for reservation through May 10' (window_opens_days carries 120), and 'you can book a maximum of 13 days beyond the last date of the reservation window'. 'For reservations less than two days in advance, please contact the park directly' - the online system stops two days out and the park takes walk-ups for whatever is left, hence after_cutoff. STAY LIMIT: 'generally limited to 14 days within any 30-day period', extendable by the park manager; a park may set less, and its entry says so (Palisade: 5 nights). No minimum stay is published. Check-in 3-10 p.m. (2 p.m. at Sand Hollow); check-out 2 p.m., noon at Wasatch Mountain, Bear Lake, Dead Horse Point, Goblin Valley, Huntington, Jordanelle, Millsite, Palisade, Quail Creek, Hyrum, Sand Hollow, Scofield and Utahraptor. A site not occupied by 10 a.m. the day after arrival is a no-show. Cancelling four or more days ahead costs an $8 cancellation fee on top of the $8 reservation fee; closer in, one night as well.

fees.note: Each entry carries its own price (Utah State Parks' fee page and the booking site). 'All reservations are charged an $8 reservation fee', non-refundable. Camping covers one vehicle's park entry; an extra vehicle pays the park's extra-vehicle fee. Bear Lake charges non-Utah residents $5 a night more; that is on its entries, not a system rule. Add-ons (2026-11-07): Entry, extra-vehicle and occupancy rules are set park by park. Goblin Valley's night includes one vehicle pass and charges $20 for an extra vehicle. Dead Horse Point includes one vehicle and charges $20 a night per extra vehicle, with eight people per site. Kodachrome charges $16 for an extra vehicle, Starvation $15, Otter Creek $25, Quail Creek $20 and Great Salt Lake $10. The state rule caps a site at the posted number of vehicles and persons. Utah's legislature sets separate fee ceilings for non-residents, but only Bear Lake was found charging them more ($5 a night).

booking.note: Tennessee State Parks' own reservation system (reserve.tnstateparks.com), or 888-867-2757. 'Reservations for campsites may be made up to one year prior to arrival date', with the whole stay, tax and the reservation fee paid at booking. The booking help on every park's page says 'Most campsites require a minimum of a 2-night stay' without saying which sites or dates, so no minimum is recorded; a one-night stay may be refused. STAY LIMIT: 'Maximum stay for camping is 14 days (28 days December 1 to February 28/29). After the maximum stay, members of the camping party must vacate the park for 3 consecutive camping nights prior to returning.' Six people per site; quiet hours 10 p.m.-6 a.m.; check-in 4 p.m., check-out noon (as printed at Tims Ford and Cove Lake). Campers no longer check in with the attendant unless a discount is applied; the site tag carries the reservation. CANCELLING: two or more days before arrival, everything back except the $5 fee; one day before, the first night, tax and the fee are forfeited; on the day, the first two nights (all of a one-night stay).

fees.note: Each entry carries its own price; Tennessee State Parks price by site, season and night, higher on weekends and busy dates, plus state and local tax. The $5 'Advanced Reservation Fee' is per campsite and non-refundable. No entrance fee. Discounts (one per site, never on premium sites): seniors 62 and over, resident or not, per the division's rate schedule when the senior owns the camper; active-duty U.S. military 25-50% (booked within 30 days of arrival); disabled visitors 25-50%; Tennessee resident veterans 50% December 1-February 28/29 and one free night on Veterans Day, and 50% year-round with a 100% service-connected disability (booked within 30 days). Add-ons (2026-11-07): No park access fee anywhere in the system. Quoted nightly rates exclude tax and the reservation fee; state and local taxes are added. Rates cover up to six people a site, with exceptions for immediate family; larger groups book another site. One wheeled camper a site at RV campgrounds.

booking.note: New Mexico State Parks book on ReserveAmerica: 'Most campgrounds have a certain number of campsites that can be reserved in advance online. Campsites can be reserved 6 months in advance.' The rest are first come, first served, and nobody may hold a site for someone else. At the campground a green 'Vacant' sign means the site is free for one night; red 'Occupied' or 'Reserved' means it is taken. STAY LIMIT (19.5.2.12 NMAC): from May 1 through September 30, 7 days in any 20-day period; from October 1 through April 30, 14 days in any 20; the director may extend, shorten or waive either. Camping gear must leave the park at the limit. A reserved site not occupied, and not called about, by 8 a.m. the day after the arrival date is released with no refund (it was 4 p.m. before the 7/1/2025 amendment). The park may require the whole stay paid in advance for weekends, holidays and special events.

fees.note: Each entry carries its own price and non-resident surcharge. Since January 1, 2025 the schedule differs by residency, per vehicle per night: primitive $10 resident / $15 non-resident; developed $15/$20; with electric $20/$30; with sewer $20/$25; electric and sewer $25/$35 (water hookups $5 more where a site has them). A site's hookup fee is owed whether or not it is used. ReserveAmerica adds $3.50 a night, at most $10 a reservation, and $5 to cancel; neither goes to the parks. Annual camping permit holders pay only the hookup fees ($5-20 a day), and a park may accept the permit at reservable sites if posted. Add-ons (2026-11-07): A camping permit covers day use of the park through 9 p.m. on the day it expires, so campers buy no separate day-use permit. Day use alone is $5 a vehicle for residents and $10 for non-residents; residents are exempt October 1 through April 30. Camping is charged per vehicle per night: each vehicle in the park overnight pays its own camping fee, and a motorhome with its towed car counts as one vehicle. The non-resident premium is $5 on primitive and developed sites; under the rule, hookup fees (water $5, electric $10, sewer $5) are the same for everyone. The division's camping page gives combined hookup prices that differ by $5-10. There is no per-person charge. The ReserveAmerica fee is $3.50 a night, at most $10 a reservation.

booking.note: MDWFP's own reservation site (reserve.mdwfp.com, a Camis system), the call center (1-800-GO-PARKS) or the park office 8 a.m.-5 p.m. 'Reservations are not required but are highly recommended especially during the peak season (May 15 through August 15)'; they are taken for 1-14 days, up to 13 months ahead, paid in full at booking. Primitive sites are not reservable. MINIMUMS: May 15-August 15, 2 nights on weekends and none on weeknights; 3 nights for Memorial Day, Independence Day, Labor Day and special events (special events carry 3 all year); 2 for Thanksgiving, Christmas, New Year's and Easter. A reserved site is released at 11 a.m. the morning after the arrival date unless the park has been told of a late arrival. STAY LIMIT: 14 days on a campsite; some parks rent designated sites by the month, up to 90 days. Check-in 4 p.m., check-out 2 p.m. Eight people and one camping unit a site (a second tent with the manager's approval, at the primitive rate); renters must be 21 or older, and the reservation holder must stay for the whole visit. CANCELLING: 7 or more days out, refunded minus the $8 reservation fee; 6 days or less, half the reservation is forfeited; within 3 days or a no-show, nothing back. Date or site changes are free up to 7 days out ($8 inside that), none within 3 days.

fees.note: Each entry carries its own price. The $8 reservation fee is non-refundable; changing the dates or site inside the 7-day window costs another $8. Park entrance is $2 a person (5 and under free) on the park pages; an RV site's rental covers fishing and the boat launch for the people registered on it, and their visitors pay entrance. Add-ons (2026-11-07): Mississippi sales tax is added where applicable. The fee schedule (40 Miss. Admin. Code Part 6, Rule 1.1) prices RV sites by the night with no per-person, per-vehicle or non-resident charge; the annual entrance pass is the same in and out of state. Eight people per site at most, visitors included; one extra tent may go on a site with the manager's approval at the primitive rate. Entrance is $0-4 a person by park (5 and under free); an RV site's rental covers fishing and the boat launch for those registered on it, visitors pay entrance, and the rules leave unclear whether registered campers do.

booking.note: Kentucky State Parks book on ReserveAmerica or by phone at (888) 4KY-PARK, up to 12 months ahead and at least a day before arrival; a campsite not reserved is first come, first served (304 KAR 1:040), and walk-ins are taken as space allows. One night is the minimum on weeknights; an arrival on Friday or Saturday must stay two, and 'longer minimum night stays are required at most campgrounds during holiday periods' (not specified, so not recorded). STAY LIMIT: 14 days, unless the park manager waives it for an emergency or business necessity. Check-in 2 p.m., check-out 1 p.m. (the regulation). Eight people and two units a site (one camper and one tent, or two tents), two vehicles; four adults and children 16 and under are in the base rate. The person reserving must be 21. Gear may not be left unattended more than 24 hours without the manager's written permission. Changes are free online or by phone up to a day before arrival. CANCELLING: 15 or more days out, the $6 reservation fee and a $10 cancellation fee are kept; 14 days or less, the first night too. On the day of arrival, call the park.

fees.note: Each entry carries its own price; parks post Sunday-Thursday, Friday-Saturday and holiday rates per site type. The $6 reservation fee is non-refundable; cancelling adds $10. Camping fees carry 6% sales tax, a 1% state transient tax and county taxes. Each adult past four on a site adds $5 a night, paid at the park. Guests 62 and over get 10% off with ID; no discounts on tent sites. Add-ons (2026-11-07): No park admission fee. Tax: 6% sales tax plus the 1% state transient tax are added to every camping fee, and county taxes on top, so the total varies by county (7% before county tax). The $5 extra-adult charge is collected on arrival at the park. Two vehicles a site at most, the RV included. Fri-Sat and holiday premiums vary by park and site type ($0-12 over Sun-Thu, holiday $0-10 more), so no flat premium fits the row.

booking.note: Arkansas State Parks' own reservation site or 1-888-287-2757, up to 12 months before arrival. By rule every campsite is reservable, a specific site included; a site not reserved is rented at the park office, and an after-hours arrival takes an open site and registers by 10 a.m. A single night is fine Sunday-Thursday; a weekend takes Friday and Saturday, and a one-night Friday or Saturday is not considered until a week out (holiday weekends excepted). Three-day holiday weekends take 3 nights. Up to 20% of a park's high-demand sites carry 3 nights on weekends (Thursday-Saturday) and 4 on holiday weekends, released on Fridays if unreserved. STAY LIMIT: 14 nights in any 30-day period at one park; the superintendent may grant 7-day extensions April-October when the campground isn't full, and longer ones November-March. Check-in and check-out are both 3 p.m. A reserved site is held until 10 a.m. the morning after the arrival date. Eight people and one camping unit a site (an RV and one tent, or two tents); an adult must register and stay for the whole period. CANCELLING: the deposit (the first night at the full rate, plus tax) is never refunded, and no refund is made for leaving early from a holiday weekend; moving the arrival date means a new reservation and a lost deposit, though nights can be added at either end.

fees.note: Each entry carries its own price; nightly rates vary by site, date and demand, plus tax and a reservation fee whose amount the site doesn't state. The non-refundable deposit is the first night's full rate plus tax, and the balance is paid on arrival. Discounts, with proof at check-in: Arkansas residents 62 and over pay half Sunday-Thursday and 25% less on weekends and holidays; out-of-state 62 and over pay 25% less Sunday-Thursday only; U.S. citizens with a 100% total and permanent disability pay half year-round. Add-ons (2026-11-07): No park entrance fee (Crater of Diamonds charges separately for its diamond search area, which is not camping). Campsites carry state and local sales tax plus the 2% tourism tax, at a rate that varies by park; the old self-pay sites were posted tax-included. Eight people per site at most, day visitors not counted; one car may park at the site and further vehicles go to designated parking, with no charge stated. No non-resident camping rate appears in the last published fee schedule (2021), but rates are now set by date and demand, so that is not recorded as a zero.

booking.note: Vermont State Parks book on ReserveAmerica, by phone at 1-888-409-7579 (weekdays 9-4) or at the park in season. Dates open daily on a rolling 11-month window at 9 a.m.; same-day bookings until 2 p.m. on the arrival day. Full payment at booking. A reservation made more than 7 days ahead needs 2 nights; inside 7 days one night is fine on any day (remote sites at Waterbury Reservoir, Osmore Pond and Kettle Pond always need 2). A booking made on the day its dates open can't be changed or cancelled for 22 days. Without a reservation you may camp if a site is open, but none are held for walk-ins. STAY LIMIT: 21 nights on most sites; 14 on prime sites at Little River and Ricker Pond and on Knight and Woods Islands; 7 for Molly's Falls Pond, Waterbury Reservoir remote sites, Burton Island waterfront lean-tos, cabins and cottages. After the limit, wait 7 days before booking another site in the same park. Check-in 2-9 p.m., check-out 11 a.m.; 8 people and 2 vehicles a site. A camper who hasn't checked in or called by 2 p.m. on the third day loses the site, without refund. CANCELLING: 10 or more days out, everything back but the $8 fee; 3-9 days, the fee and one night are kept; 0-2 days, no refund. Free date or park changes three or more days out if the number of nights and sites stays the same.

fees.note: Each entry carries its own price and non-resident rate (in effect since July 1, 2025). Site prices cover 4 people; each extra person is $8 a night (8 at most), each pet $3 a night. The $8 reservation fee is per site and non-refundable. Visitors to a campsite register and pay day-use admission ($5 adult, $2 child 4-13). Vermont residents 62 and over and honorably discharged veterans can get the $2 Green Mountain Passport (lifetime free day use, not camping). Add-ons (2026-11-07): Registered campers use the park's day-use areas free until closing on check-out day; their visitors pay day-use admission. Tax: the Vermont Department of Taxes treats bare land for a customer's tent or RV as not a sleeping accommodation, so tent and RV sites carry no rooms tax; lean-tos, cabins and cottages are priced including the 9% meals and rooms tax. The 2022 fee rule makes children 3 and under free and allows two vehicles a site with no vehicle charge; it sets one nightly rate (prime sites +$2), no weekend or holiday rate.

booking.note: Alabama State Parks' own reservation site, or the park office. 'Advanced reservations may be made up to one year in advance.' STAY LIMIT: 14 nights (31 from November 1 to March 31 at select parks), applying to the camping group and the unit alike. Check-in 2 p.m., check-out 11 a.m.; the person reserving must be 18. One wheeled camper and one tent (or two tents) a site, 8 people. A reserved site not occupied by noon the day after the first night is forfeited with all fees unless the park is told; a camper gone three consecutive days forfeits the rest. CANCELLING: up to 72 hours before midnight of the arrival date, everything back but the $5.25 fee; after that, all fees and taxes are kept (for any nights cancelled).

fees.note: Each entry carries its own price; rates vary by site and night. The $5.25 reservation fee is non-refundable, per site. 15% off nightly camping, with ID at check-in, for guests 62 and over, veterans and active-duty military, guests with disabilities (ADA), and State of Alabama employees. Add-ons (2026-11-07): Campsites carry Alabama's lodgings tax plus local lodging taxes, at a rate that varies by park (4% at Paul Grist, 17% at Oak Mountain); some parks add a resort fee (3.75% at Oak Mountain). Per-person park admission is set park by park ($3-5 an adult) and whether registered campers pay it is not stated; at some parks visitors of campers pay per vehicle. Occupancy limits (eight people, two vehicles at Oak Mountain) are posted park by park.

booking.note: Louisiana State Parks book on the Go Outdoors Louisiana system: 'Reservations can be created up to 13 months in advance online, and changed and cancelled by calling 1-833-609-0686.' The person reserving must be 21. STAY LIMIT: 15 consecutive days on any site, then 7 consecutive days away before using it again. Campsite check-in 2 p.m., check-out 1 p.m.; keep the registration receipt. Occupancy is set per site. CANCELLING: a reservation made 10-13 months before arrival costs one night to cancel; inside the 9-month window, $10 at 15 or more days out and one night within 14 days.

fees.note: Each entry carries its own price; rates rise with demand within each site type's range, plus tax. The $4.50 reservation fee is per booking. America the Beautiful Senior and Access pass holders get 50% off camping if their home state's parks honour the pass. Add-ons (2026-11-07): Rates do not include state and local taxes. A site takes one camping unit, defined as the camper plus one more vehicle; more vehicles or boat trailers park where the site manager allows. Six people per site at most. The camping fee schedule (LAC 25:IX 504) has no residency split, though it lets the agency surcharge for demand, special events or use beyond a site's capacity. Every state park also charges a per-person general admission (LAC 25:IX 500, about $3 a person, seniors and small children free), and the rules do not exempt registered campers or say whether it is charged once a stay or daily.

booking.note: IDPR's own reservation system (getoutside.idaho.gov) or 1-888-922-6743, on a rolling 9-month window, same-day bookings included. A multi-night stay booked on the first day of the window whose departure runs past it is frozen for 18 days (no changes or cancelling). STAY LIMIT (IDAPA 26.01.20.250): 15 days in any 30 consecutive days, reserved or first come; the operations administrator may set shorter or longer limits for an area. Check-in 2 p.m., check-out 1 p.m. (park time). Eight people and one RV plus up to two tents a site; one vehicle is included, others pay the $7 entrance fee. A reserved site is held until check-out time the day after arrival, then cancelled with all fees forfeited. CANCELLING (IDAPA 26.01.20.276): $10 a site before check-in time on the arrival day; after it, the first night. The reservation charge is never refunded. Changing dates so no night overlaps is a cancellation and rebooking.

fees.note: Each entry carries its own price, non-resident surcharge and $7 motor vehicle entrance fee; IDPR prices sites by demand within statewide ranges. The $10 reservation service charge is per site and non-refundable, and is waived for a camper with a current Idaho RV registration sticker; paying by card adds 3%. Discounts: 62 and over, 50% off Monday-Thursday stays (not holidays) at select parks; Idaho veterans rated 100% permanently and totally disabled get free entrance and one free campsite per stay. Add-ons (2026-11-07): The camping fee covers one vehicle for the length of the stay; a second vehicle pays the $7 motor vehicle entry fee per day ($14 for non-residents at Bear Lake, Farragut, Hells Gate, Priest Lake and Round Lake). A vehicle or trailer past the site's maximum pays an $8 overnight fee. IDPR's page gives both figures. The Idaho State Parks Passport ($10 a year with Idaho vehicle registration) covers entry, not camping or extra vehicles. Non-residents pay $3 a night more at most parks; at Farragut, Henrys Lake, Ponderosa, Priest Lake and Round Lake the non-resident campsite fee is $24-80 (Tier A). Eight people a site (16 on a companion site); the campsite fee schedule (IDAPA 26.01.20.250) charges extra people only in cabins and yurts. Posted camping fees include tax. The IDAPA amounts are maximums; the board sets the actual fees.
