booking.note: ReserveNevada (Nevada State Parks' own system since September 2023): 'Visitors may make reservations from 3 days to 11 months in advance', the window rolling at 8 a.m. Pacific. A reservable site not reserved is sold first come, one night at a time; first-come campers may extend with park staff. No minimum stay. STAY LIMIT (NAC 407.080): 14 days in any 30, less where a park's own rule says so; 14 days in 30 in the Western region bars camping at any Western-region park for the rest of the period. Check-in 2 p.m., check-out 11 a.m.; two vehicles or eight people a site; a site may not be left empty overnight without the supervisor's permission. A reserved site is held until check-in time the day after arrival, then cancelled without refund unless the park was told. CHANGES AND CANCELLING (up to 3 days before arrival): a change costs $5 more than a month out and $10 within a month; a cancellation is free (bar the $5 fee) more than a month out, $10 within a month, and $10 plus one night within 3 days. No refunds for weather, smoke, bugs, fire bans or early departure.

fees.note: Each entry carries its own price, hookup charge and non-resident surcharge. The $5 transaction fee is per reservation and non-refundable. Disabled-placard holders and active military and veterans get $1 off the daily entrance fee; no camping discount is published. Add-ons (2026-11-07): The camping fee is charged per vehicle per night at a per-park figure, so each further vehicle pays the camping fee again. A towed vehicle is free (NAC 407.055(5)), and a site takes at most two motorized vehicles, or one plus a towed vehicle, unless the supervisor allows more. Non-Nevada-registered vehicles pay $5 more per day (NAC 407.055(6)(b)). The posted camping rate is $5 higher for them, and the $10 hook-up fee is the same for everyone. Eight people a site, with no per-person camping charge in the NAC fee schedule (bike-in/walk-in entry is $2 a person). Day-use reservations made before the arrival day carry the same $5 transaction fee; same-day ones carry none.

booking.note: Nova Scotia Parks book on novascotia.goingtocamp.com or 1-888-544-3434 (519-826-5301 from outside North America); the season opens for booking all at once in spring, and the site offers cancellation alerts and a flexible-dates search up to four months out. A vacant site can be taken on arrival: at the park office at full-service parks, or by the yellow phone at the kiosk at self-registration parks (no reservation fee for a stay that starts that day). STAY LIMIT: a camping permit runs up to 14 nights on one site and lapses if the site is empty 48 hours. Check-in 2 p.m., check-out 1 p.m.; the permit holder is 19 or older and staying on the site, and a reservation can't be handed to someone else at arrival. Six people (more if one family) and one vehicle a permit. Arriving after midnight, camp one night on any vacant site and register at 9 a.m. CANCELLING: up to 2 p.m. on the arrival date, everything back but the reservation and cancellation fees.

fees.note: Each entry carries its own price (taxes included). The $8.95 reservation fee is per reservation and non-refundable; cancelling or changing costs $6.95. An extra vehicle is $8.25 a night. Seniors 65 and over and veterans (3 years' honourable service) get $2.35 a night off. Add-ons (2026-11-07): The camping permit covers one vehicle; a park attendant may permit one more where the site has room, at C$8.25 a night paid on arrival, so a motorhome towing a car pays it. Up to 6 people a site unless they are one family. Posted fees include the 14% HST (the regulation's pre-tax figures, e.g. $7.24 for the extra vehicle, are the same fees before tax). There is no park entry fee and no non-resident rate in the regulation's fee schedule.

booking.note: ReserveAmerica, online or 1-877-647-2757, up to 11 months ahead; sites open at 8 a.m. weekdays and 9 a.m. weekends on the 11-month mark. MINIMUM: 3 nights for any reservation made before April 1 of its season (so for every booking of next season); from April 1, 1 night. STAY LIMIT (Ncr 732.03): 14 consecutive days, extendable by up to 14 more when the campground is under 60% full; at Hampton Beach and Ellacoya RV parks 14 days consecutive or cumulative between Memorial Day and Labor Day weekends, never extended. Check-in 1-8 p.m., check-out 11 a.m.; only the named holder can check in, and a name change counts as a cancellation. The rate covers two adults and up to four children (at most four adults, six people). Changes by phone until the day before, $2.15. CANCELLING: 10 or more days out, everything back but the reservation fee; 4-9 days, less the fee and one night; 0-3 days, no refund. No refunds for weather or mosquitoes.

fees.note: Each entry carries its own price. The $7 reservation fee is non-refundable; a change costs $2.15. Each extra adult $10 a night, each extra child $5. New Hampshire residents 65 and over get $5 a night off the site fee as primary occupant (not on holidays or holiday-weekend minimums, and not at Hampton Beach RV, Ellacoya RV, Cannon RV or the Coleman lodges). Visitors pay the day-use fee. Add-ons (2026-11-07): At most four adults and six people a site, except in designated areas; at RV-only campgrounds no more than the RV sleeps. Tax: New Hampshire took campsites out of the meals and rooms tax in 2010; cabins and yurts are still taxed. Visitors register and pay the day-use fee.

booking.note: reserveNDparks.com or 800-807-4723 (7 a.m.-8 p.m. Central). Campsites can be booked 95 days ahead; on the first day a date opens, not before 7 a.m. Central. STAY LIMIT: 14 nights in any 30 days. Check-in 4 p.m., check-out 3 p.m. Every vehicle needs a park entrance permit, campers included. Changes online or by phone, $5, but the arrival date can't be changed. CANCELLING: more than 7 days before arrival, a $10 fee; 7 days or less, one night; no refund once the arrival date passes without cancelling.

fees.note: Each entry carries its own price and vehicle entrance permit. The reservation fee is per site and non-refundable: $6 at checkout on the booking site; NDPRD's FAQ says $5.80 online or in person and $9 by phone. A change costs $5. Add-ons (2026-11-07): Every vehicle needs a daily or annual vehicle entrance permit, campers included: $7 a day, $35 a year, $61.25 for a family annual permit (two household vehicles), one price for everyone; North Dakota residents 65+ pay $28 a year. Additional vehicles at a campsite pay the daily fee for each day in the park. A site takes one camping unit with up to six people, or the immediate family. Saturday nights cost $5 more on standard, modern and premium sites (on the entries).

booking.note: reserve.wyoming.gov or 877-996-7275 (7 a.m.-7 p.m.). Wyoming residents book up to 120 days ahead, non-residents 113; new dates, and any site freed by a cancellation, release at 7 a.m. MT. A booking made on the first day of its window can't be changed for 18 days. Reservations are taken only in each park's season (mostly May 15-September 15); outside it every site is first come, and most parks keep some first-come sites in season too. STAY LIMIT: 14 days in any rolling 30 at one park. Check-in after 3 p.m., check-out by 11 a.m.; the account holder must occupy the site every night, and a reservation covers one vehicle. Not there by 11 a.m. the day after arrival is a no-show, cancelled without refund (a third no-show cancels the year's bookings). CANCELLING: a refund only up to two full calendar days before arrival (for a Friday arrival, by Tuesday night); never for early departure, weather or low water.

fees.note: Each entry carries its own price, non-resident surcharge and day-use fee. The reservation fee is $4 for Wyoming residents and $8 for non-residents; a change is $4; none of them is refunded. Wyoming resident veterans rated 50% or more service-connected disabled camp and enter free for life with the Lifetime Veteran's Pass. Add-ons (2026-11-07): A night's charge per vehicle is the base camping fee, plus the day-use fee, plus sales and lodging tax on the base fee. The base fee is $10 for residents and $18 for non-residents. The day-use fee is $7 a vehicle for residents and $12 for non-residents. The tax runs about 10-13% depending on the park's local rate. Day use is free at Connor Battlefield, Medicine Lodge and Sinks Canyon, so campers there owe only the camping fee and tax. An electric site costs $10 a night more. A reservation covers one vehicle; each additional vehicle pays day use and camping on arrival. The non-resident reservation fee is $8.

booking.note: ReserveAmerica, online or 1-877-668-2267, 11 months ahead and up to the day before arrival (48 hours before at Macedonia Brook and Mashamoquet Brook). MINIMUM: 2 nights, except that a reservation made 1-3 days before arrival may be one night (never at Macedonia Brook). STAY LIMIT: 14 consecutive days inland, 21 at Hammonasset Beach and Rocky Neck; between stays the whole party and its equipment leave the campground for 5 days, so an RV can't be left for back-to-back reservations. An unreserved site may be taken as a walk-in ($3 walk-in fee) except at Devil's Hopyard, Pachaug's Mount Misery and Green Falls, Mashamoquet Brook (with Wolf Den) and Macedonia Brook. Check-in 1 p.m., check-out noon; two vehicles a site; the primary occupant, who can't be changed, must be at check-in and be 18. Changes before check-in, $9; none within two days of arrival. CANCELLING (through ReserveAmerica only): more than 7 days out, everything back but the $9 reservation fee; 2-7 days, less the fee and one night; under 2 days, no refund. A $9 cancellation fee also comes off every refund.

fees.note: Each entry carries its own resident and non-resident price. The $9 reservation fee is per reservation; changing or cancelling costs another $9. A walk-in pays a $3 walk-in fee. Add-ons (2026-11-07): Tax: Connecticut DRS rules that renting a campsite is renting real property, so no room occupancy or sales tax is charged on it, hookups and RVs included; cabins carry the 15% room occupancy tax. The site fee covers six people including children, the most a site takes, except that a registrant's own children under 18 may all stay for the basic fee. Two motor vehicles a site; overnight parking for more is not available. Whether a camper's out-of-state vehicle pays the day-use parking fee is not published (CT plates park free; out-of-state $6-22 a day at fee parks). No weekend or holiday rate was found.

booking.note: NJ Outdoors, the state's own booking site, up to 11 months ahead (N.J.A.C. 7:2-6.7). A campsite is reserved for at least 2 consecutive nights and at most 14; a same-night booking is taken by phone, 8 a.m.-4 p.m. A person or family may hold at most two non-consecutive camping reservations at once. CANCELLING (7:2-6.8, 17.2): a refund needs at least 24 hours' notice, less a cancellation fee of $40 or two nights, whichever is less ($50 or two nights for non-residents).

fees.note: Each entry carries its own resident and non-resident price. Cancelling costs $40 or two nights, whichever is less ($50 for non-residents). New Jersey residents 62 and over, or totally disabled, get $2 a night off family campsites. Add-ons (2026-11-07): Every campground reservation, walk-ins and in-person bookings included, pays a $5 transaction fee on top of the park use fee, and a change costs $5. Family campsites are $20 a night for NJ residents and $25 for non-residents, the same every night (the fee schedule in N.J.A.C. 7:2-17.2 has no weekend, holiday or per-person charge). Two vehicles of any type may park at a site at no charge; more park in designated lots at $5 a night each. Pets $5 a night. At most six people a site unless they are all one family. No sales tax or occupancy fee on campsites (Tax Topic Bulletin S&U-13). Summer parking fees ($5-20 a vehicle a day, Memorial Day to Labor Day, N.J.A.C. 7:2-17.1) are not stated to apply to campers.

booking.note: Arizona State Parks' own booking site or 877-697-2757: up to 365 days ahead and at least one day before arrival. MINIMUM: 2 nights on peak-season weekends. STAY LIMIT: 14 nights in any 30 per park, per household (the park manager may extend). Up to five sites per household per stay. Check-in 2 p.m., check-out noon; ten people (six adults) and one vehicle a site, extra vehicles $15 a night. A camper not there by noon the day after the first night forfeits everything and the site goes to walk-ins. Two free changes; a third means cancelling and rebooking. CANCELLING (by phone, 8 a.m.-5 p.m.): a $20 fee always, plus the $3.60 reservation fee; after 2 p.m. the day before check-in, one night as well.

Add-ons (2026-11-07): The camping fee includes park entry and day-use areas for the registered stay. A day-use fee paid within 24 hours before camping may be credited toward camping; annual passes are not. Campsite fees cover one vehicle; each additional vehicle is $15 a night and must fit in the site's parking. A site takes up to 10 people, at most six of them adults (14 and older), with no per-person fee. The fee schedule has no non-resident rates. Lake Havasu and Patagonia Lake charge more for weekend and holiday day use, but camping includes entry. Peak-season weekends have a two-night minimum.

booking.note: The ParksNL Campsite Reservation Service (nlcamping.ca, or 1-877-214-2267 from 7 a.m. to 11:30 p.m.) usually opens in the third week of April for the whole season; same-day bookings until 8 p.m. Newfoundland time. Sites are sold by the night, the week, the month or the season. Any free site can be taken at the park checkpoint without a reservation, for up to 7 nights. Check-in 3 p.m., check-out 2 p.m.; the person reserving must be 16 and one occupant must be named; six people (more for one family) and one camping unit a site. CANCELLING a stay under 8 nights: free the day before arrival or earlier; on the arrival day (until 2 p.m. the next day), one night is kept; after that, a no-show with no refund. Stays of 8 nights or more: full refund 2 days out, 75% the day before, 50% on the arrival day. Changes $6, none within 3 days of arrival on a long stay.

fees.note: Each entry carries its own price and vehicle pass ($7 a night per vehicle, or $50 for the season at every park). The $7 reservation fee (HST included) is per booking and non-refundable; a change is $6 and cancelling in time is free. Newfoundland and Labrador residents 65 and over get 35% off campsite and vehicle fees. Add-ons (2026-11-07): Every motorized vehicle entering a provincial park needs a vehicle entry pass on top of the campsite permit: C$7 per vehicle for a night of camping, C$10 for day use, or C$50 for the season at every park; so a motorhome towing a car buys two. Up to 6 people a site, except family groups (parents and children under 18). The $7 reservation fee includes HST; the posted campsite and pass prices don't say.

booking.note: CampWithME.com or 800-332-1501 (207-624-9950 from outside Maine; weekdays 9-4). The season opens for booking on fixed dates in early February (Lily Bay and Sebago a few days before the rest) and reservations close for the year in mid-September; after that every site is first come until the parks close in mid-October. Book by 4 p.m. Eastern at least a day before arrival. MINIMUM: 2 nights on a Friday-Saturday stay booked before July 1; from July 1 single nights, weekends included. STAY LIMIT: 14 nights per person per park from the last Saturday in June to the third Saturday in August; no limit the rest of the season. Six people a site, one adult 18+; check-in 1-9 p.m., the camping day ends at 11 a.m.; a site may not be left more than two nights. A reserved site is held the first night, then resold at 1 p.m. on the second day with no refund. CANCELLING: before 4 p.m. on the arrival date, everything back but the processing fee; after that, the first night too. A partial cancellation can't break the minimum.

fees.note: Each entry carries its own resident and non-resident price (Maine residents hold a Maine driver's licence or vehicle registration). The non-refundable $5 processing fee is charged for each night reserved, not once per booking. 9% lodging tax on camping fees. Add-ons (2026-11-07): The camping fee includes the park's day-use fee; visitors pay day use or show a season pass. Site fees are for parties of six or fewer, and a larger party must book a group site. The 9% lodging tax is charged on all camping fees. booking.note: ReserveAmerica, up to 12 months ahead and for the same day. As of October 2026, 2027 reservations are on hold while RIDEM picks a new reservation provider, so the channel and rules may change. Unreserved sites are let first come at the parks. STAY LIMIT: 14 nights in any 21 days in peak season (the Thursday before Memorial Day through Labor Day weekend), then 7 nights away; 21 nights in 28 the rest of the year. RIDEM's full policy also sets peak-season minimum stays, not recorded here. Check-in 1-10 p.m. (no later, reserved or not), check-out 11 a.m.; the permit holder is 18 and stays on the site; one family, or six people, a site; two vehicles. The site must be occupied the first night or it is resold with no refund. CANCELLING: 8 days or more before arrival, everything back but the reservation fee and an $8.75 cancellation fee; 2 to 7 days, one night is kept as well; under 2 days, no refund. No refunds for weather or leaving early.

fees.note: Each entry carries its own resident and non-resident price (by the customer's state of residence). $8.75 reservation fee, non-refundable, and $8.75 to cancel; a second vehicle pass is $12. Add-ons (2026-11-07): The daily rate covers six people and one vehicle pass (the drivable camping unit or the vehicle towing it); a second car pass is $12 a reservation, two vehicles a site at most. Visitor passes are $8 a vehicle a day, at most two at a time. Walk-ins pay no reservation fee. Tax: the Division of Taxation rules that sites where campers bring their own tent or RV carry neither sales nor hotel tax; cabins supplied by the campground carry 7% sales tax plus 6% hotel tax. The rate table has one rate a night, no weekend or holiday premium.

booking.note: sepaq.com or 1-800-665-6527. The whole stay is paid when booking (instalments without interest for stays more than 90 days out costing $500 or more). A minimum number of nights may be required depending on the park and the season; at most 14 consecutive nights. CHANGES (same kind of site, same season): up to 5 days before arrival, free if the value is the same or higher, $7 plus tax if lower; within 4 days, and on arrival day before 3 p.m., one change only, at 50% of any decrease (minimum $14). CANCELLING: up to 5 days before arrival, refunded less $7 plus tax; within 4 days, no refund. The terms always follow the original booking, even after a change of dates.

fees.note: Add-ons (2026-11-07): Corps camping fees are per site and include the site's amenities, utilities and the cost of recreation.gov, so there is no reservation fee (recreation.gov's $10 change/cancellation service fees still apply). The camping permit covers the project's Corps-run day-use areas (boat ramps, beaches) on the days it is valid. Vehicles parked on the site within its posted carrying capacity (people, vehicles and camping units, set per site by the project, often 2 vehicles and 8 people) cost nothing extra. A vehicle in separate improved parking may be charged a parking fee, and a registered camper's day visitors may be charged up to 50% of the site fee.
